SPEC DEVIATION to decide (unchanged since c3/e4, kept by dec-mv3vui7s-014f6e7c): spec Supersession > Replan says 'after commit, the handler drains the queue for affected requests (the reconciler also drains it)'. Today only the reconciler drains (2 entries per tick, every RS_RECONCILE_INTERVAL_MS, default 15 s), so after a supplier change, a refusal or an admin fault the customer sees replanning/'Finding a new plan with current stock…' for up to one interval. c3's tests (supplier-orders.test.js) assert replanning right after the change, so an immediate drain in src/routes/supplier.js would also need those tests changed. The planner is synchronous CPU work (150-800 ms), which argues for leaving it in the tick. Recommend recording this as an accepted deviation, or a follow-up for f4/g3.

A superseded or refused request has the NEW version only after a drain; the view in between is replanning (4a) or, while a void is outstanding, cancelling (4). While a void is outstanding the request keeps reading cancelling (WAIT) even after the drain stored the new version (row 4 precedes rows 4a and 12); the new version is already currentPlanId then, and the old orders are in cancellingOrders. The UI should offer Approve only once the rescue status says REVIEW_NEW_PLAN or APPROVE_PLAN (f3 already does).
